templateNote: Meeting notes are organised by outcome, not by speaking order: what happened, what was agreed, what was only proposed, who does what, and what is still unknown. Agreements and proposals never share a frame.

frames.title: What happened
frames.purpose: The cause, timeline and impact, and the three gaps the meeting found.
frames.rationale: The findings explain the decisions; they are facts, not outcomes of the meeting.

frames.title: Agreed decisions
frames.purpose: Only what the meeting explicitly agreed.
frames.rationale: A reader must be able to trust that everything here was agreed.

separateFrom.reason: Agreed and unagreed items must never be mixed.

frames.title: Proposed, not agreed
frames.purpose: Proposals that were discussed but not agreed, with the disagreement and their status.
frames.rationale: Keeping them apart from decisions is the point of the case.

frames.title: Action items
frames.purpose: Who does what, by when — exactly as stated.
frames.rationale: A checklist is the natural form for action items.

frames.title: Open questions
frames.purpose: Questions the meeting raised and left unanswered.
frames.rationale: An unanswered question must look unanswered, not be folded into a finding.

elements.content: A 16:40 config typo set the connection pool from 50 to 5 (meant 55); alert 17:02, rollback 17:15, recovered 17:27 — 47 minutes, about 2,300 failed checkouts, 140 tickets
The alert fired as configured (10% for 15 minutes), which is too slow for checkout
The status page went up at 17:20, 40 minutes after errors began, because the incident commander posts it when they remember
Config changes skip code review: code needs two approvals, config none
Agreed: checkout error-rate alert at 5% over 5 minutes
Agreed: support can post status-page updates directly, without waiting for the incident commander
Agreed: payments config moves into the repo; every change gets a pull request and one payments-team approval

elements.role: proposal with its disagreement and status
elements.content: Tomás proposed no payments deploys after 15:00 on Fridays; Leila disagreed (it moves the risk to Monday; the cause was the missing review); not agreed and not decided
elements.layout: One card: the proposal, both sides of the disagreement, and its status. The status is not a separate card.

elements.content: Marcus proposed automatic rollback when checkout errors double within 10 minutes of a deploy; Leila is wary of database migrations; left open
elements.layout: May equally sit in the open-questions frame; never with the decisions.

elements.content: Marcus: alert change by Wednesday, March 19 · Leila: config into the repo with an approval rule by Friday, March 21 · Tomás: six months of incident data for the review on April 2 · Kenji: draft the customer email (no deadline given)
elements.layout: A checklist; owners and dates live in the item text (canvas.todo has no owner or due-date fields).

elements.content: Unknown: were any of the 2,300 failed checkouts retried successfully? Nobody has checked the payment logs; the answer changes the customer email

relationships.explanation: The new threshold answers the 22-minute detection.
The review rule answers the unreviewed config change.
Letting support post answers the late status page.

together.reason: The three explicit agreements form one list a reader can trust.

keepSeparate.reason: Both are about preventing a repeat, and Leila argued review, not the day, was the cause; merging them would make the freeze read as agreed.
Both concern the error rate; only the threshold was agreed.
Leila said auto-rollback might suit config; that is not part of the config decision.

hierarchy.reason: The finding explains the decision; it is not weighted above it.
